title: LCK Enters Warring States Era, Halting Gen.G's Reign - 조선일보
content: Gen.G secures third straight regular season title but faces T1, Hanwha Lifee in playoffs amid intensified competition LCK (League of Legends Champions Korea) has entered a 'Spring and Autumn Warring States period' after five years. LCK concluded its 2026 regular season on the 23rd and will enter the postseason starting on the 26th. Due to participation in the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, the regular season was reduced by one round compared to last year. Gen.G secured the regular league title for the third consecutive year, including the 2024 spring and summer seasons. However, this season's notable trend was that Gen.G, which had established itself as the 'sole powerhouse' in the regular league over the past two years, showed signs of instability in performance from the early stages of the season, leading to a rare intense competition where the top spot was only confirmed in the final match. For the first time in five years since the 2021 summer season, there was no absolute powerhouse dominating the league. Both the 'Legend Group' consisting of the top five teams and the 'Rise Group' made up of the bottom five teams in rounds 3–4 engaged in fierce competition for rankings until the final stages. Gen.G suffered a 1–2 comeback defeat against DiPlus KIA in the final regular season match held on the 22nd. Gen.G took the first set, giving them an advantage in set differential and head-to-head record against second-place Hanwha Lifee Sports. However, they lost the next two sets, securing the top spot somewhat awkwardly. This was a far cry from Gen.G's dominant performance last year, where they suffered only one loss in the single-season format, and two years ago, when they had one loss per season during the split spring and summer seasons. While the team's morale was shaken by late reports of tax evasion allegations surrounding captain 'Ruler' Park Jae-hyuk at the beginning of the season, a more fundamental analysis points to the improved counterplay from opposing teams. Although the current roster has been cohesive for two years, making their teamwork even stronger, opposing teams have accumulated more data and experience to analyze Gen.G. Additionally, the ever-changing meta made it difficult for Gen.G to consistently maintain their previous strengths. The growth of rival teams cannot be overlooked. T1, the eternal rival, showed fluctuations in performance due to fatigue from participating in various international tournaments like MSI and EWC, yet still maintained top-tier competitiveness. Hanwha Lifee Sports, which has formed a three-way power structure with Gen.G and T1 since two years ago, also continued to deliver consistent performance, including an MSI championship, and competed with Gen.G for the top spot until the end. Although Gen.G did not dominate as they did in the past two years, the numerous trials and errors experienced amidst fierce league competition hold significance as they prepare for the playoffs and subsequent international tournaments. Particularly, if Gen.G aims to reach the Worlds (League of Legends World Championship) final and secure the title, which they have yet to achieve since their rebranding, addressing the weaknesses and variables exposed during this season's regular league has become a crucial task. Gen.G has directly advanced to the second round of the playoffs. The winner of the final match between Hanwha Life and T1 on the 23rd will also proceed directly to the second round, while the losing team and fourth-place DiPlus will begin the postseason in the first round of the playoffs. Prior to the playoffs, the 'Play-In' stage will feature KT Rolster, ranked fifth in the Legend Group, facing the top three teams from the Rise Group: Hanjin Brion, BNK Piorx, and Nongshim Red Force. Two teams that survive the Play-In, held from the 26th to the 28th, will join the playoffs.

title: Top Court Upholds Antitrust Fine Against GS Retail - Seoul Economic Daily
content: The Supreme Court has ruled that a fine of about 1 billion won ($720,000) imposed by South Korea's Fair Trade Commission (FTC) on GS Retail, the operator of GS Home Shopping, was justified, finding that the retailer improperly returned goods to suppliers and unfairly passed on promotional costs. The confirmation of the FTC's corrective order and fine is expected to influence trade practices across the country's retail industry. According to legal sources on the 23rd, the third division of the Supreme Court, with Justice Roh Kyung-pil as the presiding judge, upheld the lower court's ruling that had rejected GS Retail's lawsuit against the FTC seeking to overturn the corrective order and other measures. An FTC investigation found that GS Retail violated the Act on Fair Transactions in Large Retail Business by returning about 62,000 items worth around 1.85 billion won ($1.3 million) between April 2017 and October 2019, based only on removal request forms from suppliers. Under the law, a large retailer may not return all or part of goods it has received without justifiable cause. However, in the case of direct purchase transactions, justifiable cause is presumed when a supplier voluntarily requests the return in writing before the return date, attaching objective evidence that the return directly benefits the supplier. The commission also confirmed that GS Retail made suppliers bear the cost of sales promotion events held from January 2015 through 2018 without a prior written agreement on cost-sharing. In addition, from January 2018 to June 2020, it had professional broadcasters, entertainers and others affiliated with suppliers appear as guests or models on home shopping broadcasts without a written agreement on the terms of their dispatch. The FTC ordered GS Retail to pay a fine of 1.027 billion won and issued a corrective order. GS Retail contested the decision and filed a lawsuit. FTC rulings such as sanction decisions carry the same effect as a court's first-instance judgment. As a result, administrative lawsuits concerning fair trade cases and the FTC begin at the Seoul High Court as the first instance, under a two-tier system that then proceeds to the Supreme Court. In May last year, Division 6-2 of the Seoul High Court found the FTC's disposition lawful. The court held that a supplier's request for a return based on documents alone was not enough to accept it as a voluntary request. It cited the fact that GS Retail, during the FTC investigation, had signed a written statement acknowledging that suppliers had borne the cost of sales promotion events without a prior written agreement. The court also considered that 556 of the 562 supplier employees flagged by the FTC were found to have been made to work at GS Retail's own business sites in violation of the Act on Fair Transactions in Large Retail Business. The second-instance court explained that "it is reasonable to view this as conduct in which a large retailer used its superior bargaining position to unfairly impose disadvantages, entrenching abnormal trade practices and posing a significant risk of undermining fair trade," adding that "the FTC's calculation of the fine cannot be seen as an unlawful abuse or deviation of discretion when compared with the gravity of the violations." The Supreme Court upheld the lower court's judgment, finding "no error affecting the ruling, such as misapprehending the facts underlying the calculation of the fine or violating the principles of proportionality and equality." The ruling confirms the fine and corrective order imposed on GS Retail. Analysts say the decision could accelerate efforts to improve unfair practices in the retail industry. title: Supreme Court upholds FTC fine over GS Retail’s unfair costs to SMEs in Korea - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
content: Top court backs antitrust order penalizing GS Retail for pushing costs onto small suppliers The Supreme Court ruled that the Korea Fair Trade Commission's corrective order and a 1 billion won penalty surcharge against GS Retail for unfairly shifting expense to suppliers were justified. The Supreme Court's Third Division (presiding Justice Noh Kyung-pil) said on the 23rd that on the 9th it finalized a lower court ruling dismissing GS Retail's suit to cancel the corrective order against the Korea Fair Trade Commission. GS Retail absorbed GS Home Shopping in Jul. 2021. The transaction at issue occurred at GS Home Shopping. Home shopping companies sell products to consumers through broadcasts. When consumers who watch the broadcasted product sales place orders with a home shopping company, the company asks a supplier to deliver the product to the consumer. The home shopping company deducts part of the payment made by the consumer as a sales commission and pays the remainder to the supplier. However, the Korea Communications Commission, to expand sales channels for small and midsize enterprises, evaluates the share of direct purchases of SME products when a home shopping company seeks renewal of its program provider license. Because of this, home shopping companies directly purchase SME products and, when orders arrive, deliver them to consumers. In this case, the inventory burden falls on the home shopping company, not the supplier. From Apr. 2017 to Oct. 2019, GS Retail returned 62,399 directly purchased products from eight SMEs. The purchase amount was 1.85622 billion won. GS Retail did not specifically agree on return conditions when contracting with suppliers. Of the returned products, GS Retail sent back 6,001 items after receiving only a take-out request from suppliers. It returned 56,398 items after receiving a take-out request and documents that included a resale plan. Also, from Jan. 2015 to Nov. 2018, GS Retail conducted sales promotion events—such as free gift promotions and product review events—while selling products supplied by 26 SMEs through broadcasts. At that time, GS Retail made suppliers bear the sales promotion expense. Additionally, from Jan. 2018 to Jun. 2020, while airing 505 broadcasts for products supplied by 144 SMEs, GS Retail had 562 people—supplier-affiliated employees or hired professional broadcasters, entertainers, models, and sales experts—work in its broadcast studio. For these reasons, the Korea Fair Trade Commission (FTC) found that GS Retail violated the Act on Fairness in Large Retail Business and in Jan. 2022 imposed a corrective order along with a 1.027 billion won penalty surcharge. GS Retail filed an administrative suit, arguing the disposition was unjust. In court, GS Retail argued, "Suppliers voluntarily requested returns in writing, attaching objective supporting materials that returns would benefit them." It also said it did not pass on sales promotion expense to suppliers, and that suppliers had their employees appear on home shopping broadcasts for their own benefit. The Seoul High Court dismissed GS Retail's claim. The panel said that in direct-purchase transactions, for returns, suppliers must refund payments already received, incur additional distribution expense, and then resell the products, adding that "suppliers have very little incentive to request returns." It continued, "Based solely on the evidence GS Retail submitted, it is insufficient to find that suppliers voluntarily requested returns." The panel also ruled on the disposition imposing a 1.027 billion won penalty surcharge, saying, "GS Retail's act of prohibiting product returns involves a violation amount of 1.8 billion won, which is by no means small," and "the calculation of the penalty surcharge did not deviate from or abuse discretion compared with the seriousness of the violation." The Supreme Court dismissed GS Retail's appeal, finding the lower court did not misapprehend the legal principles.

title: Supreme Court Finalizes 1.027 Billion Won Penalty for GS Retail's Unfair Returns and Cost-Shifting - 아시아경제

Supreme Court Finalizes 1.027 Billion Won Penalty for GS Retail's Unfair Returns and Cost-Shifting The Supreme Court has finalized a penalty of 1.027 billion won imposed on GS Retail for unfairly returning products to suppliers and passing on promotional event expenses to them. Supreme Court, Seocho-gu, Seoul. Photo by Yonhap News Agency According to the legal community on August 23, the third division of the Supreme Court, presided over by Justice Roe Kyungphil, recently upheld a lower court ruling dismissing GS Retail's suit against the Fair Trade Commission seeking to annul corrective orders and penalties. Previously, the Fair Trade Commission had issued a corrective order, a notification order, and an order to pay a penalty of 1.027 billion won. The commission found that from April 2017 to October 2019, GS Retail violated Article 10, Paragraph 1 of the Large-scale Retail Business Act by returning a significant number of products to suppliers only after receiving a request for removal, rather than properly documenting the returns process. Furthermore, from January 2015 to November 2018, the company was found to have violated Article 11, Paragraphs 1 and 2 of the same law by carrying out promotional events, such as offering gifts, and shifting the associated costs to suppliers without any prior written agreement on cost sharing. Additionally, from January 2018 to June 2020, GS Retail was judged to have violated Article 12, Paragraph 1 by allowing professional broadcasters and entertainers hired by suppliers to work as broadcast guests and models without a written agreement on dispatch conditions. The key points of contention were whether the request forms or official documents obtained by GS Retail from suppliers constituted objective supporting evidence for the legitimacy of the returns. It was also disputed whether guests employed by suppliers who appeared on GS Home Shopping broadcasts qualified as employees under the law, and whether such broadcast appearances could be considered as labor performed by dispatched employees. Furthermore, there was debate over whether the calculation of the penalty exceeded the Fair Trade Commission's discretionary authority. The appellate court ruled against GS Retail. It found that merely requesting product returns based on a removal request form was insufficient to recognize the voluntary nature of the suppliers' requests for return. Of the 562 employees mentioned by the Fair Trade Commission as working for the suppliers, it determined that 556 were recognized as having worked at the business location in violation of Article 12 of the Large-scale Retail Business Act. The court also found no illegality in the calculation of the penalty. It noted that the amount involved in the violation of the product return prohibition was considerable, at around 1.8 billion won, and that a large-scale retailer like GS Retail using its superior transactional position to impose undue disadvantages would risk normalizing abnormal business practices and significantly undermine fair trade. © The Asia Business Daily. title: 2026 Vikings vs. Ravens Preseason Game Observations - Minnesota Vikings
content:
MINNEAPOLIS — Waves of reserves competed for roster spots and roles as Minnesota hosted Baltimore in the second preseason game of 2026 to conclude a productive week packed with purple. The Ravens prevailed 13-3 by keeping the Vikings off the score board in three separate quarters and taking advantage of a drive that was extended by a roughing-the-passer penalty in the second half. Vikings Head Coach Kevin O'Connell and Ravens Head Coach Jesse Minter opted to rest starters Saturday after having those groups take the brunt of practice reps on Wednesday and Thursday during joint sessions. J.J. McCarthy opened and experienced a couple different ups and downs, playing only the first quarter behind an offensive line of Henry Byrd, Joe Huber, Michael Jurgens, Vershon Lee and Ryan Van Demark from left tackle to right tackle. The opening possession started at the 12 after a special teams penalty on the opening kickoff. McCarthy's first throw on an out to Myles Price was high and hot. A false start penalty put Minnesota in second-and-15 from the 7, and McCarthy worked his way out of that with back-to-back 8-yard completions to Tai Felton and Price for a fresh set of downs. The run game, however, didn't start as fast as it did in Minnesota's preseason opener. Rookie Demond Claiborne was stuffed for no gain on his first carry and a loss of 3 a play later. The Vikings were unable to convert third-and-13 on a pass to Felton that gained 8. McCarthy's second series featured the highlight of his day but ended with a lowlight. On second-and-7, he navigated through the pocket, evading a rusher and launched a 50-50 ball to Felton, who secured the catch for a gain of 50 to the Baltimore 10-yard line. McCarthy followed by working through the progression over to Claiborne for a catch-and-run of 7. A pass on second-and-goal at the 3 screaming toward Felton (it needed to be a hard throw) was not secured, and a Claiborne run on third down gained nearly 2. Minnesota opted for a shotgun formation pass on fourth down, and McCarthy had Price open but missed him. A little less mustard would have done the trick. The Vikings had two more series with McCarthy at QB. One play after a sack by Mike Green, McCarthy drilled a pass to Jeshaun Jones for a gain of 19 despite taking a hit. It would have converted third-and-14, but Byrd was flagged for holding, creating a third-and-23 on which Claiborne ran for 9 before a punt. The Vikings committed a false start on their fourth possession. McCarthy took a hit for the fourth time but was accurate with a pass to Price on third-and-13, but Chandler Rivers was credited with a pass defensed. McCarthy finished 5-of-10 passing for 81 yards and a 77.5 passer rating before he was replaced by Carson Wentz in the second quarter. View game action photos from the Vikings preseason game vs. the Ravens at U.S. Bank Stadium. Wentz played two series, including a 2-minute drill to close the first half. He picked up third-and-8 during the drive with a 9-yard pass to Dontae Fleming before firing to Jones for a gain of 35. Jones completed the catch despite an initial bobble and contact that sent him to the turf. Vikings Offensive Coordinator Wes Phillips, who called plays the entire game (O'Connell normally does), dialed up a beautiful tight end screen to Gavin Bartholomew. Walter Rouse got down the field from the left guard spot and absolutely pancaked defensive back Amani Oruwariye to spring Bartholomew for a gain of 16. A sack on second-and-8 from the 27 led Minnesota to opt for a 52-yard field goal by Will Reichard to tie the game at halftime. Wentz finished 9-of-11 passing with 92 yards and a passer rating of 101.5. The Vikings continued evaluating veteran punter Johnny Hekker and rookie Brett Thorson, who held for the long field goal by Reichard. Thorson did not hold at Georgia, so this is the first time he's been tasked with that role, by the way. He punted two times for a gross average of 41.5 with a long of 42 (which means his other was 41), pinning Baltimore inside its 20-yard line with both punts. Hekker punted three times for a gross of 165, averaging 55.0 and uncorking a long of 65 to help flip field position when Minnesota was backed up. Many parts of the box score were not too dissimilar, but the turnover margin was Minnesota at minus-2. The Vikings lost a fumble after a short catch on the third play of a possession that spanned the late third quarter and start of the fourth. Baltimore capitalized on getting the ball on the Vikings side of the field and added a field goal to make it 13-3. Max Brosmer was leading the offense down the field in the fourth quarter but a possession that covered 57 yards ended on the 11th play when Brosmer was intercepted by Silas Walters. Brosmer finished 11-for-17 with 98 yards and a passer rating of 55.5. The longest run allowed by the Vikings went for 8 yards on a scramble by QB Joe Fagnano. Minnesota reserve RB Jermar Jefferson produced the game's only run of 10 or more yards when he got loose for a gain of 15. title: GS/OS was Apple’s Colorful Desktop That Lived on the Wrong Machine from the 1980s - TechEBlog -
content: Most people who remember personal computers from the late 1980s think first of the Macintosh and its clean black-and-white interface. Apple had already shipped something that looked and behaved a lot like it, only this version ran in color on a machine that still carried the Apple II name. That system was GS/OS, and it arrived in 1988 as the heart of Apple IIGS System Software 4.0. GS/OS was built from the start in 100% 16-bit code for the 65816 CPU inside the IIGS, which was a significant shift from previous versions. Most other software on this computer was still inadequately optimized for 8-bit routines carried over from the previous Apple II generation. The improved code resulted in significantly faster disk access, screen rendering, and program loading. Customers who had upgraded from ProDOS 16 were particularly affected. The No. 19 Stephen Cameron Racing Ford Mustang GT4 of Gregory Liefooghe and Sean Quinlan earned its first Michelin Pilot Challenge GS victory at Virginia International Raceway (VIR). Liefooghe recorded the fastest lap of the race with a time of 1:54.154. The No. 60 KohR Motorsports Ford Mustang GT4, driven by Mike Skeen and Evan Slater, finished second — the team's third GS podium finish across its entries in the last two events at VIR. The No. 64 TeamTGM Ford Mustang GT4 of Ted Giovanis and Hugh Plumb were awarded the Bronze Cup. GREGORY LIEFOOGHE, No. 19 Stephen Cameron Racing Ford Mustang GT4 – 
   “I have trouble finding the words to describe what this means. We’ve been working so hard on this program, to be able to do this. The Ford Mustang GT4 has been fast in a lot of races, but we’ve had a little bit of bad luck here and there. It’s just amazing to get a Ford one-two finish. The Mustangs were truly fast. [Sean] Quinlan did amazing and having Racing to End Alzheimer’s on the car makes it extra special. This one is for Steve Cameron and Racing to End Alzheimer's.” SEAN QUINLAN, No. 19 Stephen Cameron Racing Ford Mustang GT4 –
    “It’s such a relief to get a win today. We’ve been close so many times, and so many things can go wrong. Finally we had a race where everything went to plan. [Greg] Liefooghe did an awesome job. We knew our Ford Mustang GT4 was great and Greg was fast, and when he got in he just started passing cars one by one, which looked promising. The yellow threw in a moment of doubt, but he pulled it off and took the lead just before the second yellow.” MIKE SKEEN, No. 60 KohR Motorsports Ford Mustang GT4 –

 “I did a lot of fuel saving on my stint to try to get us to that window where we could make that happen, and we lucked out to get those last yellows. Evan [Slater] had done a great job getting us up front and into a podium position to begin with, and then I just had to keep our Ford Mustang GT4 up there. Big gamble, but the car was really strong and it worked out today.” EVAN SLATER, No. 60 KohR Motorsports Ford Mustang GT4 –
    “It’s my second podium and the highest I’ve finished in an IMSA race, which is an amazing feeling. It was a ton of fun out there in the Mustang. We didn’t have the best qualifying, starting the race eighth, but I made my way up to first on the track. There were a lot of two-wide moments and a lot of tough battles. I’m just so thankful to be here and to Mike [Skeen], Ray Mason and to all the KohR Motorsports guys for making this possible.”
